_about: The 50 pages to build first for Google clicks in Nov 2026 - Mar 2027, ranked by a stated model. Written 2026-10-16 by an analysis pass; nothing here is scheduled or built. Read next-50.md for the method, the evidence and the verdicts. Estimates are model outputs with wide ranges, not measurements.

method.demand: Google Trends, United States, weekly, 2024-10-01 to 2026-10-10, pulled 2026-10-16 through Trends' own data endpoint (rate-limited, retried with waits). Every request compared up to four terms with the same anchor, "stink bug"; ratio = term average / anchor average. Nov-Mar factor = the term's Nov-Mar average / its average over the whole window; for terms below 0.06 the weekly values are 0-3 on Trends' scale, so the factor is taken from the parent topic instead.
method.calibration: 12 terms with stored Ahrefs US volumes give about 175,000 Ahrefs searches per ratio unit (spread 52,000-310,000). Where this site ranks 6-8 in the US for an exact phrase, Search Console shows 4,000-10,000 US impressions a month per ratio unit: Ahrefs overstates what this site can see by roughly 20-40x.
method.model: clicks per month (Nov-Mar average, page live by mid-November) = 10 x sqrt(ratio / 0.0895) x NovMar factor x format factor x SERP factor x Search Console factor; range x0.4 to x3.
method.base: 10 = the site median new page (12 clicks/month by month 3 in season, CLAUDE.md, measured Oct 14) x 0.85 for the ramp from a mid-November launch.
method.reference: 0.0895 = median ratio of 8 keywords of the 86 US guides measured in the same Trends run (a typical guide-sized topic scores 1.0).
method.sqrt: bigger topics have harder results pages; in their first five days the small long-tail guides out-collected head terms (bugs-that-look-like-cockroaches 665 impressions, flying-ants 23).
method.searchConsoleFactor: 1.3 when the site already shows for the topic: a Canadian edition with 1,000+ impressions in 90 days at an average position of 10 or better (for US editions), or 100+ impressions at position 10 or better on the page's own kind of query (product queries do not count); else 1.0
method.serpCheck: 37 Google results pages (gl=us, hl=en, pws=0) read in the built-in browser on 2026-10-16 until Google showed its unusual-traffic page, which was not bypassed. A few more were read with the WebSearch tool (a different engine; marked per page).
method.searchConsole: Session pull of 90 days to 2026-10-12 (single-dimension query pulls, all countries and US); the API token has since expired (invalid_grant).
method.autocomplete: Google autocomplete (hl=en, gl=us), from an Ontario IP: proves demand exists and lists variants; gives no volume.
method.overlap: Existing routes (app/blog, app/learn, content/guides, next.config.mjs redirects) and the section headings of the overlapping guides were read; every proposed slug is free.
method.money: Owner's Mediavine assumptions from Oct 14: about $20 blended and $30 US per 1,000 sessions, 1.3 ad-page sessions per Google click.

totals.note: sum of the 50 per-page estimates, clicks per month averaged over Nov-Mar, pages live by mid-November

buildWaves.note: Rank = expected clicks; waves also weigh timing, dependencies and confidence.

why.1: start now: the strongest estimates, the two topics in season right now (Asian lady beetles peak in November; winter house bugs in December-February), the rat pair, and the look-alike pages that the species pages will link to
why.2: next: the large spider, flea and cockroach pages and the three state pilots, early enough to read the pilots by Jan 31; read the recluse-bite results page on Google before writing that one
why.3: then: big but authority-led or summer-leaning topics, and the smaller rodent pages
why.4: last: hubs after their spokes, conditional pages (springtails, cockroach droppings) and the smallest topics
